environment.description: Same application deployed to an internal AKS cluster (1.28). The Kubernetes Ingress is handled by an nginx-ingress-controller (v1.9.4) configured with annotation nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/auth-tls-verify-client set to 'on' and auth-tls-secret pointing to a namespace-scoped Secret containing the internal CA bundle (corp-pki-ca-chain). The ingress terminates TLS and performs client certificate verification against the corp PKI CA chain before forwarding any request to the backend pod. Client certificates are issued only via the internal HashiCorp Vault PKI engine (pki_int/issue/app-client role) with a 4-hour TTL, and the role constrains allowed_domains to '*.corp.internal' with enforce_hostnames=true. The Vault policy for obtaining these certs requires entity membership in the 'directory-api-consumers' identity group, which is manually managed by the platform team. Additionally, the AKS pod runs with a NetworkPolicy that only permits egress to the LDAP server on port 636 (LDAPS), and the AD DS server requires channel binding (LdapEnforceChannelBinding=2) and LDAP signing.
